html:
SMTO-RST-0007 — This can't be deleted while work in it is still unfinished

GUID: bacbbd55-80a7-4b80-a479-a6dace16c4f9
Slug: run-retention-protected
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • SMTO didn't delete this because a task in it is still running, queued, waiting for your answer, or has a step whose outcome isn't settled yet. SMTO keeps those records until the work ends.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation and stop any running task with Stop current task, or let it finish. A running task still needs its records, so SMTO keeps them until it ends.
  2. Answer or decline any question or approval the task is waiting on, and remove unstarted prompts with Delete queued task. Waiting and queued tasks count as unfinished work in this conversation.
  3. Check that every task shows as finished or stopped, and that what you wanted to delete is still there, before deleting again. This confirms the earlier delete didn't already happen and that nothing still needs those records.

What success looks like

  • The delete completes and the item no longer appears in your list.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before you try anything again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove SMTO's data files by hand to force the delete; unfinished work still needs them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Deletion or retention found active or unresolved owners (queued, running, waiting or interrupted chat tasks, a blocked lane, pending steers, unknown operations or unsettled jobs) that still depend on the conversation's records.

What this means

  • Retention/deletion finds active owners, pending/unknown operations, unsettled jobs or queue/steer state that still depends on the conversation's evidence. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Retention/deletion finds active owners, pending/unknown operations, unsettled jobs or queue/steer state that still depends on the conversation's evidence.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact active jobs, unknown operations and lane ownership before requesting deletion.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the conversation's tasks, jobs and unresolved operations (assert_chat_deletable, memory_retention purge, task store delete). Stop or reconcile them through the existing controls, confirm the earlier deletion did not already apply, then request the deletion again.
  • Inspect active jobs and unresolved operations. Stop or reconcile them through the existing controls before deliberately deleting their retained evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported settlement/reconciliation removes blockers while preserving needed execution evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
